chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Mukkan, from Ishaq al-Madaini, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who board a ship, purchase food, and take possession of it, then one of them buys it and they ask him to give them whatever food they desire, so the owner of the food is the one who delivers it to them and receives the payment. He said: 'There is no harm, as I see them as having shared with him.' I said: 'If the owner of the food comes and calls a measurer to measure it for us, and another person among us measures it for him, causing it to be weighed/measured and thus increasing or decreasing (the amount), he said: 'There is no harm as long as it is not a large amount of error.'

key_terms.يُعَيِّرُهُ: he measures/weighs it (often implying using a specific measure or causing variation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food that is still on a ship or in the possession of others?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *bay' al-madmun* (sale of goods in transit), establishing that when a group entrusts one member to purchase food, they become co-owners (*shuraka*) of the bulk purchase, allowing for individual distribution. The Imam further refines the commercial law by permitting minor measurement errors (*ghalat*) during the weighing process, provided they do not constitute significant deception, thereby balancing practical trade needs with fairness. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for validating complex supply chain transactions where goods are not yet in the direct possession of the final buyer.
